title.narrative: Output 2.2. Increased capacity of Member States to apply international labour standards

description.narrative: The Committee of Experts on the Application of Conventions and Recommendations (CEACR) in its 2023 report noted with satisfaction the information provided by the Government of Eswatini regarding the submission on 25 May 2022 to the Senate and on 23 May 2022 to the House of Assembly of ten instruments adopted by the Conference at its 99th, 100th, 101st, 103rd, 104th, 106th and 108th Sessions (2010–19). The Committee commended the efforts made by the Government of Eswatini in meeting its constitutional obligation of submission of standards adopted by the ILC to the competent authority for consideration. The instruments concerned include the 2014 Protocol to the Forced Labour Convention, 1930, the Violence and Harassment Convention, 2019 (No. 190), the Forced Labour (Supplementary Measures) Recommendation, 2014 (No. 203), the Transition from the Informal to the Formal Economy Recommendation, 2015 (No. 204), the Employment and Decent Work for Peace and Resilience Recommendation, 2017 (No. 205), and the Violence and Harassment Recommendation, 2019 (No. 206). Since the submission of the ten instruments to Parliament (Senate and House of Assembly), the ILO at the request of the Government of Eswatini has commissioned a gap analysis of Eswatini law and Practice in respect of C190. Following training on the provisions of C190 in February 2023, the Workers Organizations (the Federation of Eswatini Trade Unions and the Trade Union Congress of Eswatini) have developed a Joint Work Plan. The Joint Work Plan adopted by the trade union leadership in March 2023, includes an action item to lobby and promote advocacy for the ratification of C190. In the previous biennium, the ILO sensitized the Government of Eswatini on its outstanding ILO constitutional obligation to submit to Parliament instruments adopted by the International Labour Conference from its 99th up to and including its 108th Sessions. In May 2022, the ILO provided advisory support to the Ministry of Labour and Social Security to avert the inclusion of Eswatini in the list of Member States in a situation of serious failure to meet their Constitutional obligation of submitting ILO instruments to the competent authorities for consideration after their adoption by the ILC. To this end, the ILO provided guidance on the format of the formal communication required under the ILO Constitution on the action taken to submit ten Instruments to Parliament for consideration. Such guidance is provided in the Memorandum Concerning the Obligation to Submit Conventions and Recommendations to the Competent Authorities.

Output 2.2. Increased capacity of Member States to apply international labour standards

description.narrative: The Government of Eswatini and the Social Partners developed the 2nd generation Decent Work Country Programme (2022 – 2025) within the framework of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF 2021 – 2025) for Eswatini. Cabinet approved the Decent Work Country Programme (DWCP) in October 2022, and Government and the Social Partners officially launched the DWCP in November 2022. The DWCP includes output 1.1, 1.2 which explicitly address issues raised by the ILO CEARC. Output 1.1 states that Government and the social partners apply relevant tools and undertake empirical research to ascertain the feasibility of setting a National Minimum Wage and to ensure that Minimum Wage Schemes are free from gender bias. And this output addresses the Direct Request of the CEARC adopted in 2019 on C100; Output 1.2 states, Government and the social partners address the gender pay gap by instituting policy measures to promote equal remuneration for work of equal value. This output addresses the CEARC Observation adopted in 2019 on C100. Output 3.3 of the DWCP states that the tripartite partners have an improved understanding of their reporting obligations and take decisive action to address the comments of the ILO supervisory bodies, including those pertaining to C182 and 138. The text in the strategy for Outcome 3 in the DWCP specifies that the Social Partners’ capacities to engage with Government in addressing comments on the application of ratified Conventions will constitute a significant aspect of support provided. Once the UNSDCF was adopted and launched in October 2020, the ILO resumed support to a tripartite drafting team for the DWCP between May 2021- November 2021 for the formulation of the DWCP, including sensitizing them on the ILO’s cross cutting policy drivers and the centrality of the ILO’s normative standards to the DWCP. In June 2022, the ILO facilitated an online session for the tripartite DWCP drafting team to provide sensitization on the comments of the ILO’s CEACR and to discuss inclusion of text pertaining to issues raised by the ILO’s CEARC into the draft DWCP. The issues integrated were taken from the CEARC reports on C100 published in 2019.
